User question (verbatim context): Is there a pattern in how the stock market goes before and after US midterm elections? Specifically, if the midterms flipped both House and Senate against the president's party (user believes President, House, Senate currently Republican; VERIFY), what does historical evidence say? Market has rallied sharply in recent days; user asks whether it is a known pattern that markets spike until the election then drop, or whether it depends on outcome. Today is 2026-10-07; midterms are 2026-11-03. User is a long-term investor. Bundle 01 items: (1) S&P 500 return and max intra-year drawdown in midterm years vs other presidential-cycle years; the Q3 trough and Q4 rally pattern. (2) Returns in the 3/6/12 months after midterm elections; Sep-Oct low to year-end stats; post-WWII sample size and dispersion by year. (3) Pre-election 3-month vs post-election returns; how reliable/statistically meaningful is the pattern (small n, confounders).

Mode: INITIAL (write a new report from scratch). QUICK-mode depth budget: at most ~8 WebSearch/WebFetch operations total, survey-level answers, 2-3 strongest sources per question; flag unknowns rather than digging further. Link every empirical claim to a source URL with date; give specific numbers (averages, medians, sample sizes, ranges) not vague summaries; state uncertainties and counter-readings explicitly. Write the report to reports/2026-10-07-midterm-election-market-patterns/individual/01-midterm-cycle-seasonality.md
